Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the NovaRetail Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for queuing questions will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to NovaRetail's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, COO; and Riley Patel, CMO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of NovaRetail.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 performance, driven by evolving customer purchasing habits that boosted order frequency and robust promotional strategies that accelerated sales momentum. We saw significant growth in key metrics, including GMV up over 20% year-over-year.

Our focus remains on enhancing customer retention through subscription models and AI-driven personalization. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our expanded private-label offerings, which we believe will significantly improve margins over time.

We are investing heavily in supply chain automation and regional expansion to support this growth.

Finally, we are committed to balancing aggressive customer acquisition with profitability discipline.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Our Q3 revenue was $27.0 billion, an increase of 19% year-over-year and 6% quarter-over-quarter. This significantly outperformed our guidance from the Q2 call, where we had projected 15% to 17% YoY growth, implying roughly $26.0 billion to $26.4 billion—we beat the high end by over $600 million. This marks another quarter of accelerating top-line momentum, underscoring the strength of our marketplace ecosystem, logistics scalability, and AI personalization.

Diving deeper into revenue drivers, marketplace revenue—which includes GMV take rates from third-party sellers—grew 23% YoY to $19.8 billion, or 73% of total revenue. GMV itself rose 22% YoY to $195 billion, outpacing industry peers. Third-party services like fulfillment fees through our ShopNova Fulfillment Network expanded 26% as penetration reached 67% of units. High-margin categories shone: electronics up 29% on AI device demand, beauty up 25% via influencer and TikTok shoppable integrations.

First-party retail revenue grew 9% YoY to $4.4 billion, with improved inventory turns at 13x annualized. Advertising revenue surged 33% to $2.2 billion, benefiting from our generative AI recommendations that lifted click-through rates 19% and AOV 13%. Subscription and services, powered by ShopNova Prime with 190 million members up 15% YoY, grew 16% to $550 million, with same-day delivery at 44% of Prime orders thanks to micro-fulfillment and EV fleets covering 88% of major U.S. markets.

Regionally, North America drove 62% of growth, U.S. revenue up 21% to $17.7 billion amid reaccelerating discretionary spend. Europe grew 17% to $5.1 billion constant currency, gaining market share despite DSA regs, with ultrafast grocery pilots adding $350 million. APAC accelerated 26% to $3.1 billion, led by India festive prep and Southeast Asia live-streaming. Latin America contributed 13% YoY to $1.1 billion, with Mexico up 47%.

QoQ, the 6% sequential growth topped our implied 4-6% guide, aided by back-to-school and easier comps. Mobile app orders hit 74%, conversions up 10% via NovaAI analyzing trillions of signals, AOV steady at $50.

I'll now dive into our customer metrics, focusing on order frequency, which came in at 2.6 orders per active customer, up 24% year-over-year from 2.1. This is the strongest quarterly acceleration since Q2 2021's pandemic peak of 2.8. Our 12-month trailing frequency stands at 9.8, showing sustained improvements in purchasing habits in a maturing e-commerce market.

Cohort-wise, recent 12-month acquires—our highest-CAC group amid competition from Instacart and DoorDash—hit 1.7 orders in first six months, up 15% YoY. These newer customers build stickier habits post-trial. Legacy 2020-2021 cohorts stabilized at 3.2 quarterly orders, supported by ShopFast Unlimited at 68% penetration driving 42% of orders.

Key drivers included inflation pushing value repeat buys, with 12% more pantry staples like essentials akin to Amazon Basics. AOV held at $58, frequency offsetting macro basket compression. Seasonal back-to-school and holiday gifting spiked 31% week-over-week in late August for families, similar to Walmart and Target trends. Apparel replenishment rose 18% YoY as Shein supply issues let us gain with AI wardrobe bundles. Softness hit discretionary electronics, down 5% for non-subscribers due to longer cycles like Best Buy noted.

Technically, RFM modeling and GenAI Habit Loops—using reinforcement learning like Alibaba's—prompt micro-reorders, e.g., Tide pods restocks with 20% off Subscribe & Save, yielding 28% conversion lift and 35% second-order boost in 30 days. Frequency Rewards in ShopFast, with free expedited over $25 after three monthly buys like Instacart Express, hit 22% adoption and 16% bump in tests. Edge computing with AWS enables sub-2-hour delivery in 15 metros via micro-centers, boosting urban frequency 41% YoY against DoorDash DashMart.

Regionally, U.S. led at 2.9 orders with 75% Prime parity and Sun Belt same-day. Europe at 2.1 faced VAT but rebounded 19% sequentially post-Brexit, strong UK via Tesco bundles. APAC hit 3.4 for 88VIP-like subs on Singles' Day, Southeast Asia at 2.0 improving 22% MoM via Lazada.

These gains lift LTV to $1,240 from $1,050, CAC payback to 8.2 months from 10.4. We're shifting 60% of $150M FY24 marketing to loyalty, as each order adds $12 gross margin. Q4 frequency to 2.8 on BFCM personalization, subscription flywheel at 52% GMV insulating vs. rate hikes like Chewy Autoship.

Promotions were pivotal, accounting for 62% of QoQ GMV growth to $2.8 billion overall, though scaled across our larger base—up 22% YoY and 8% QoQ. Over 1,200 campaigns including flash sales, bundles, and AI-personalized codes lifted promoted units 28%, AOV steady at $85 via 12% basket upsell. Fashion/beauty GMV up 35% mimicking Shein drops, electronics 18%. Active customers to 45 million, 40% new from promo traffic on Google Shopping/TikTok.

Promo spend $68 million up 18% YoY, 2.4% of GMV, contracting gross margin 310bps to 28.5% from markdowns at 22% off and $35 free shipping. Fulfillment up 90bps to 14.2%. Yet adjusted EBITDA held at 11.8%, down 150bps, via dynamic pricing capping 25% discounts for high-LTV, preserving 85% full-price. 30% promos to loyalty via Retail Rewards (65% retention, 2.5x LTV), cutting repeat CAC 22%.

North America (45% GMV $1.26B) disciplined at 1.8% intensity, 25% sales lift/100bps dilution. Europe (28% $784M) 32% growth/400bps pressure vs. Zalando. APAC (22% $616M) 45% sales/520bps hit offset by 15% last-mile cuts. Evolving to smart stacking with 15% better ROI, 20% subscription-tied promos adding $120M recurring. H2 promo GMV 20-25%, margins 28-29% via 500M profiles. Net: $1 invested yields $4.60 GMV, ROAS to 5x.

Gross margin was 38.5%, up 230bps YoY from 36.2% and 80bps QoQ from 37.7%—fifth straight expansion, TTM 37.9%, best since 2021 IPO. Over two years, up from 34.8% low: Q1'22 35.1%, Q2 35.4%, etc., 370bps organic gain outpacing Wayfair/Etsy peers.

Mix shift (140bps): Electronics/home to 42% GMV at 45-48% margins, apparel down to 22% at 28-32%. Private label to 28% revenue at 52% margins (vs. 35% third-party), NexBasics kitchen/wellness up 45% units via Vietnam/Mexico mfg saving 8-10% COGS. Supply efficiencies (60bps): 5-7% COGS cuts on top SKUs, turns to 8.2x, NexPredict AI cut stockouts 30%.

Headwinds: Shipping up 12% to 9.8% mitigated by 65% in-sourced NexShip; promos/returns offset by dynamic pricing/computer vision (25% refund cuts); FX/tariffs via India shift. NA 39.8% (+300bps), EMEA 36.2% flat, APAC/LatAm 34.5% (-50bps). Q4 38.7-39.2%, FY 38.1% via GenAI bidding, BOPIS, eco-labels.

Gross margin drivers tie to promos. Operating expenses were $8.5 billion, representing 31% of revenue. Marketing spend was up 12% to $285 million with 5.8x ROAS.

Net income was $1.3 billion, or $2.75 per share. We ended with $16.2 billion in cash. Reaffirming full-year guidance of $108-110 billion revenue, 38% gross margin.

Now I'll turn it over to Taylor Kim to discuss operations.

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Jordan. Operationally, we focused on supply chain resilience and fulfillment scalability. Shipping times improved by 25% to under 24 hours for 70% of orders. Fulfillment costs declined 18% per unit to 12% of GMV. We are implementing robotic sortation in 250 centers and drone hubs in 20 markets, cutting delivery costs 23% YoY.

Now I'll turn it over to Riley Patel.

Riley Patel:
Thanks, Taylor. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from Nova Everyday multimedia on TikTok/Instagram with UGC #NovaStyleChallenge, and advantage+ shopping on Meta/TikTok. Customer acquisition costs were $28, down 16% YoY. Brand awareness increased by 28% to 42% unaided recall per Nielsen.

Total spend $285 million, ROAS 5.8x best in years. Brand recall up via 2.1B impressions, 78% video completion, CTV on Hulu/Roku 3.2x lift, Google search +22%, DCO cut CPV 19%. New customers 4.2M up 18%, CLV/CAC 4.1x.

Paid social 45% acquires 7.2x ROAS, AOV $72; search 25% 6.1x conquering Amazon; affiliates 15% $19 CAC 8.4x; email 15% win-backs. NA 22% growth 6.4x, EMEA 12% 11% efficiency, APAC 42% 4.9x, LATAM 25%. Privacy-first CDP 85% match, NovaAds RMN next Q $50M run-rate. Q4 ROAS 5.5-6x, 15-20% new growth.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Instructions for the question and answer session: Please press star then one on your touchtone phone if you would like to ask a question. Our first question comes from Mike Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Chen:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On order frequency, can you expand on the regional variances and how ShopFast is driving LTV?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Mike. As Jordan detailed, U.S. at 2.9 with strong Prime parity, Europe rebounding, APAC leading on subs. ShopFast's 68% penetration and rewards are key to LTV at $1,240, payback under 9 months—we see it insulating through holidays.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with JPMorgan.

Lisa Wong:
Great results. On promotions, how are you managing margin pressure into Q4 with holiday intensity?

Jordan Lee:
Lisa, thanks. We structured promos for efficiency—loyalty focus, smart stacking pilots at 15% better ROI. H2 GMV lift 20-25% with margins stabilizing 28-29%, ROAS to 5x. Subscription upsells adding recurring revenue balance it out.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Ruiz with Morgan Stanley.

David Ruiz:
Impressive gross margin expansion. What are the biggest levers for Q4 and beyond?

Taylor Kim:
David, fulfillment in-sourcing and AI forecasting are core, as I noted—turns up, costs down 18%. Private label scale and mix shifts add 140bps tailwinds, positioning us for 39%+.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Park with Barclays.

Emily Park:
On marketing, how sustainable is the CAC decline with privacy changes?

Riley Patel:
Emily, our first-party CDP and clean rooms ensure 85% match rates post-cookie. Channels like affiliates and live-streaming in APAC deliver sub-$25 CAC with high AOV—Q4 15-20% new adds at steady ROAS.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
